WITH cv_index AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS index_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca
    ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
   AND ca.ancestor_concept_id = 134057 -- Disorder of cardiovascular system
  WHERE co.condition_start_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY co.person_id
), cats AS (
  SELECT * FROM (VALUES
    (134057, 'Cardiovascular'),
    (320136, 'Respiratory'),
    (432250, 'Infectious'),
    (4201745, 'Digestive'),
    (75865, 'Urinary/renal'),
    (376337, 'Nervous system'),
    (4244662, 'Musculoskeletal'),
    (31821, 'Endocrine'),
    (436670, 'Metabolic'),
    (432586, 'Mental/behavioral'),
    (317248, 'Hematologic'),
    (440371, 'Immune')
  ) AS v(concept_id, category)
), post_dx AS (
  SELECT co.condition_occurrence_id, co.person_id, co.condition_concept_id
  FROM cv_index i
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co
    ON co.person_id = i.person_id
   AND co.condition_start_date > i.index_date
   AND co.condition_start_date <= DATEADD(day, 90, i.index_date)
)
SELECT TOP 20
  cats.category,
  COUNT(DISTINCT post_dx.person_id) AS patients,
  COUNT(DISTINCT post_dx.condition_occurrence_id) AS diagnosis_records,
  CAST(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT post_dx.person_id) / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cv_index),0) AS decimal(5,2)) AS pct_of_cv_cohort

Using OMOP `condition_era`, I defined the cardiovascular index event as the first era under acute MI, cerebrovascular accident/stroke, heart failure, or cardiac arrest descendants. The cohort contained 133,404 patients. Diagnoses starting >0 and ≤90 days after the index date were grouped by SNOMED ancestor categories.

| Rank | Diagnosis category within 90 days | Patients | Diagnosis eras | % of CV-event cohort |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Cardiovascular | 58,139 | 263,278 | 43.58% |
| 2 | Metabolic | 30,716 | 69,188 | 23.02% |
| 3 | Respiratory | 24,160 | 67,074 | 18.11% |
| 4 | Nervous system | 21,498 | 52,019 | 16.11% |
| 5 | Digestive | 20,755 | 52,730 | 15.56% |
| 6 | Urinary/renal | 19,332 | 50,313 | 14.49% |
| 7 | Musculoskeletal | 17,190 | 41,172 | 12.89% |
| 8 | Endocrine | 16,513 | 27,446 | 12.38% |
| 9 | Infectious | 14,965 | 33,021 | 11.22% |
| 10 | Mental/behavioral | 13,604 | 25,001 | 10.20% |
| 11 | Immune | 8,739 | 14,491 | 6.55% |
| 12 | Hematologic | 4,028 | 6,712 | 3.02% |

Biological relationship analysis from the KG showed that these post-event diagnosis groups are not independent comorbidity buckets; they share substantial disease-gene architecture with cardiovascular disease:

- Nervous system disease: 3,185 shared CV-associated genes; examples include `ADORA2A`, `FLNA`, `BMPR1B`, `VHL`, `GNAQ`, `KCNK3`, `CDH13`, `CACNB4`.
- Musculoskeletal: 2,517 shared genes; examples include `FLNA`, `BMPR1B`, `VHL`, `EIF2AK4`, `STING1`, `KCNK3`, `HNF1A`.
- Digestive/GI: 2,494 shared genes; examples include `FLNA`, `BMPR1B`, `VHL`, `GNAQ`, `STING1`, `SLC22A3`, `CDH13`.
- Metabolic disease: 1,836 shared genes; examples include `FLNA`, `VHL`, `GNAQ`, `KCNK3`, `SLC22A3`, `ARHGAP42`, `NECTIN2`, `HNF1A`.
- Endocrine disease: 1,801 shared genes; examples include `ADORA2A`, `FLNA`, `VHL`, `GNAQ`, `KCNK3`, `HNF1A`.
- Respiratory disease: 1,658 shared genes; examples include `FLNA`, `VHL`, `EIF2AK4`, `GNAQ`, `STING1`, `CDKN2A`, `CAV1`.
- Urinary/renal disease: 1,544 shared genes; examples include `FLNA`, `VHL`, `HNF1A`, `COL4A1`, `SLC22A2`, `NDUFAF6`.
- Immune disease: 1,457 shared genes; examples include `STING1`, `HNF1A`, `CDKN2A`, `SMARCA4`.
- Infectious disease had fewer direct shared disease-gene links, 528, but still connected through inflammatory and host-response genes such as `HLA-B`, `C3`, `NFKBIA`, `AGTR1`, and `CAV1`.

Interpretation: the dominant 90-day diagnoses after cardiovascular events are recurrent/ongoing cardiovascular disease plus cardiometabolic, pulmonary, neurologic, renal, and infection-related complications. The KG links support plausible shared biology: vascular injury and thrombosis, inflammation/immune activation, hypoxia, neurovascular sequelae, kidney–heart metabolic coupling, and endocrine/metabolic risk pathways. Caveat: this is an observational EHR count of diagnosis eras, not causal incidence; categories can overlap because SNOMED ancestors are hierarchical.
